newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche 9-mo gp net profit up 9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche 9-mo gp net profit up 9 pct.

text.p: (in millions of marks unless otherwise stated)
Group profit after taxes 1,530 up 9.1 pct
Net profit per 5-dmk share 2.95 vs 2.75 dmk
NOTE - Full name of the German bank is Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank. Earnings compare with first nine months of 1995.
The net profit is below analysts' forecasts which had averaged 1.7 billion marks. Deutsche's net profit had risen 15 percent at the half-year stage.
Forecasts for Deutsche's operating profit after provisions averaged 3.62 billion marks and ranged from 3.58 billion marks to 3.68 billion. Deutsche is not holding a news conference.

Analysts had predicted Deutsche's earnings would suffer from added risk provisions to cover the injection of 180 million pounds sterling into its British unit Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), hit by irregularities at three unit trusts which came to light in September.

Deutsche is the only German bank to publish under the more transparent International Accounting Standards. Other banks are also moving to broader disclosure but are still publishing their accounts exclusively according to the German Commercial Code (HGB).
Group return on equity before tax 14.3 pct vs 12.4 pct
NOTE - Balance sheet total and all items listed below it compare levels at Sept 30, 1996 with December 31, 1995.
Deutsche Bank said the 21.8 percent rise in balance sheet total was explained by increased activities in investment banking.
The bank said listed securities in its financial holdings on September 30 had a book value of 38.3 billion marks and a market value of 57.6 billion marks.
